item.title: Re: Seeking greenlighting (or something idk i'm new here)
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi Ked Stand. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I have a few issues with this concept, but at the same time, do take my comments with a grain of salt as I think it boils down to personal taste:

The object has too many anomalous properties, making it both overpowered, amalgamous and worst, unexplained. Is there a reason why you’ve assigned so many disparate powers to a single watch, such that it can reset time, pause time, give you a boost of energy and attach itself permanently to the user? It sounds as though you’ve simply tried to attach as many properties as possible to the object in order to make it sound cooler. Unfortunately, that’s not how we advise new writers to craft their scps.

Choose one (or two, max) anomalous properties and then try your best to explain how they function and why. You’ve got a discovery and test logs outlined already, but notice we don’t see any hint of who created this watch or what its designed purpose is.

tldr: pare down the anomaly to its main, most exciting qualities, then try to explain its backstory before proceeding. Again, this is just my opinion. Feel free to look for other reviewers if you want another. But if you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi Galcedion. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So I like the fact you’re attempting to write a sci-fi scip, doubly so that it involves horror. My main problem with the concept is that it’s the basic plot of almost every Hollywood alien movie out there, mainly: crew goes on a mission, encounters alien they don’t understand, get murdered one-by-one etc. At this point, the genre is tried, tested, and cliqued, to be honest.

I know you’ve tried to give the alien more distinguishing characteristics, but still, the other dimension aspect is from Event Horizon, the melting of the crew into the walls is a page lifted from Aliens. What I’m saying is that the best way to distinguish a sci-fi scip from others is know what’s already out there and have a different origin story of your entity, if you’re sticking with the horror. Right now, you’ve said it’s “unknown”, and that just won’t cut it either. Encourage you to expand on this a little more.

If you decide to revise the concept / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll take another look. For now, all the best!

item.title: SCP-XXXX (Gestalt Suffering)
item.content:encoded:
Foundation personnel encounter anomalous bio-hazard which rewrites the memories of exposed individuals.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article w/ GRU-P GoI Formats As well

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch:
- SCP-XXXX is a contagious biohazard developed by GRU-P as a mass amnestic to be deployed against target populations in conjunction with large scale cognitohazardous propaganda campaigns.
- SCP-XXXX does not produce the intended affect, instead, all individuals exposed to SCP-XXXX have memories and personality traits changed at random, developing personality traits and memories of other individuals afflicted by SCP-XXXX, living or dead.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
Foundation Personnel are initially unaware of the anomalous properties of SCP-XXXX when it is first encountered, instead mistaking it for a conventional biohazard developed by Soviet Researchers at Aralsk-7/Vozrozhdeniya Island. After several incidents, however, Special Containment Procedures are developed. The discovery and containment of SCP-XXXX will be told thru interviews and incident reports focusing on the mental and emotional challenges Foundation Personnel must overcome, particularly the afflicted, who are able to observe and experience the destruction of their identities without knowing exactly what is going on.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Due to the proliferation of chemical and biological weapons at former Soviet Weapons Site/GRU-P installation Aralsk-7, discovery and containment is a unique challenge for the Foundation due to risks posed by other SCP’s at that location as well as conventional hazards and the involvement of other GoI’s (Namely UN/GOC). Story will have heavy focus on the tragedy which sometimes befalls Foundation Personnel in the pursuit of their mission.

Additional Notes:
Would love advice on formatting as well as dramatic storytelling through otherwise clinical Foundation interviews and incident reports. Also, any guidance on GRU-P formatting/storytelling also welcome. Thanks!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: SCP instance naming
item.content:encoded:
so what exactly is this for?

Basically any sort of specific thing that is related to a primary anomaly, but distinct enough to make more sense to mention specifically. So if the Foundation was containing an anomalous field and there was an anomalous rabbit that only shows up in that field, the field would be SCP-XXXX and the rabbit would be SCP-XXXX-1. That helps prevent confusion/strange sentences where it would make sense to refer to only one thing at a time (for example, "SCP-XXXX-1 consumes solely dandelion greens" makes sense for the rabbit, not the field).

additionally I'm wondering if something like SCP-XXXX-1-1 would be acceptable or if it should just be referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

It depends on what relationship that something has to SCP-XXXX-1. You would use an offshoot that has an existing designation offshoot number if you're referring to a specific part of that previously designated thing. To use the previous example, if the rabbit carried a good luck charm that had its own anomalous properties, that might be SCP-XXXX-1-1, though I think most authors would use SCP-XXXX-1-A or SCP-XXXX-1a or the like.

So basically:

  • SCP-XXXX: main anomaly/main collection of anomalies the Foundation is containing
  • SCP-XXXX-1: part of/a component of SCP-XXXX
  • SCP-XXXX-1-A: part of/a component of SCP-XXXX-1
  • and so on.

I don’t think it’s a balrog. If I were down in a burning coal mine fleeing for my life from a giant horned fire monster I wouldn’t stick around long enough to get a good look at it, especially since most of its body is probably obscured by smoke anyway. It’d be easy to confused among all the smoke and fire given off by the creature itself and the burning coal around it, so it’s no surprise that reports vary as to its appearance. A LotR fan is already going to expect a balrog when encountering a fire demon in an abandoned mine, so they’ll be more likely to mistake random shapes in the fire and smoke for wings and the iconic weapons. It’s just human pattern recognition at work.

item.title: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action/Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP format with an extended incident log

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation works hard to cover up anomalies, having extensive measures to prevent word of the Paranormal getting out. But the internet is a popular thing, especially among conspiracy theorists.

Central Narrative: A simple anomaly is discovered by WWS. It's a frog that when a picture is taken of it, always produces the same photo. Further more, whenever an addition copy of the photo is created, physical or digital, a non-anomalous frog of the same type is formed in the vicinity. The main story of the article comes when a member of the Parawatch community gets their hands on one of the photos and discovers it's properties. They send it to the rest of Parawatch who continue to send it and copy it like crazy. The Foundation learns about it but their normal strategies such as taking the picture down and visual amnestics don't work due to the paranoia of Parawatch and them saving copies to hard-drives. This comes to a head when the Foundation resorts to a complete take-down of the Parawatch wiki and the physical administration of amnestics to all exposed members, draining significant resources and giving the Parawatch community a lot to speculate on. The article closes out with a note regarding the difficulty of maintaining the veil in the internet age and about being thankful the image wasn't memetic.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A simple anomaly and a non-anomalous group almost breaking the veil.

Additional Notes: I am considering adding an interview with a Parawatch member, but am unsure if the Foundation would do that sort of thing.

item.title: Negative-Safe Entity
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Intrigue

Page Layout (Optional): Typical SCP article, including interview with the Dr that initially specified designation.

Elevator Pitch: Just a regular person that wants to be secured, contained, and protected.

Central Narrative: They are found having snuck into a containment cell for a Euclid class before it arrived.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: They keep hijacking foundation assets to produce containment cells for themselves, so they get an SCP article where there special rules are "get them out of the cell" since they make good cells quickly and cheaply relative to proper channels.

Additional Notes: Ties in with many other SCPs (by having their cells made by this entity), unique "history" for main entity.

Original Motivation: Originally thought of by imagining the "box" analogy. Many edge-cases are covered (e.g. thaumiel class), but what about if the entity would enter the box if not prevented? I pictured a gas that had to be expunged, but didn't find a good story there, eventually ended up with this. Still Safe class though.

item.content:encoded:
I have edited the initial post based on your feedback. :)

+ show block
– hide block

He's not an all-knowing unstoppable monster… just a man who sees a little more than others, with an obsession that may or may not be justified, and a few tricks up his sleeve.

This is a part of the vibe that I am trying to create. In a one on one scenario, Twist can be very intimidating. However, put a couple more people in the room and he is far less deadly and easier to contain due to the nature of how his anomalous traits work, which I planned to explain in the article.

What if he can see the potential in things, too?

The short answer would be yes. So long as the object is within his line of sight, he can view this.

A laundry list of abilities isn't going to interest the audience

I completely agree. Anything he has in his arsenal I already have inventoried. It's not going to be a batman utility belt scenario. I have some stories in mind for this character within the SCP universe with a few of them focusing on how he got some of his artifacts. However, one of the critiques that I get here is that the one ability I do mention (instantly knowing things about stuff he sees) is boring/uninteresting or broken. He does have other capabilities that I haven't mentioned here, but I haven't mentioned them because they aren't crucial to the story or to what the story is supposed to be focusing on, which is supposed to be about the SCP foundation trying to get information out of Twist and figuring out the rules to obtaining this information. So, to placate the critique of "uninteresting anomalous ability", I mentioned a few other items/powers. In response to your review in particular though, I have since removed them.

It seems clear there was no malicious intent, but the fact is that many of these infomercial products are attempts to market mobility aids to the general public, and knowing that makes this a very uncomfortable read. item.title: The Monastery of the Weaponsmith (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action, History

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, Weapons of the monks, Entry attempts

Elevator Pitch: A monastery in the mountains, guarded by six warrior monks that possess incredible strength and speed, and have anomalous weapons, made from unknown materials. The source of these weapons is the monastery they guard.

Central Narrative: Foundation agents try to enter the monastery for investigation purposes, but the monks halt their attempts. Each monk has a unique weapon: a spear, a bow, shield & sword, javelins, greatsword and a glove, capable of pulling and pushing objects. They use different formations and tactics to defect all attempts at attacking them, or entering the monastery. From the monastery, sounds of smithing, woodcutting and working can be heard, and the monks state that the foundation "must not disturb the weaponsmith".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The weapons are made from unknown materials, and possess anomalous properties, such as size change or appearing out of thin air. Much like the materials, the maker of the weapon is unknown aswell. The monks are anomalous aswell, possessing grey skin and eyes with a purple glow.

Additional Notes: The article would feature an log describing the attempts that the Foundation made to enter the monastery. In it, the different tactics would be described, used by the monks, for example, the bowman shoots the grenades out of the sky while the shieldman defends him, etc.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Monastery of the Weaponsmith (seeking greenlight)

I have a little bit of a theory/headcanon about this…

So, the containment procedures mention a weird bit about a humanoid appearing:

Once a month, a humanoid entity will appear on the border of Threshold Yuf and inform personnel of any adjustments that must be made to these containment procedures. These instructions are to be followed without question, and the entity is then to be executed using a gunshot to the head.

While the containment procedures are strange, this part in particular stands out as being rather strange.

Another interesting thing is how our poor friend Julius managed to come up with these seemingly perfect containment procedures in just a week. Seems an impossible task, but he achieved it, didn't he?

Well, what if he didn't?

See, what if the ritual he designed isn't for the containment of the object, but containment of Julius Green? See, he complained about not having enough information about what he was containing, so why not contain what he could?

But why would he contain himself, you ask? Because he needed more time. He sort-of tricked O5-6 by providing him with containment procedures but also providing himself with more time to do his job.

What I'm getting at is: the figure that appears is some form of Julius Green getting reborn/appearing as a ghost/etc. to add to the containment procedures. He contained his soul/consciousness with some kind of ritual, that allows him to return in the future to update and perfect the ultimate containment procedures.

I have no clue if this is the actual truth of how this all works or anything but I like it :)

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Responding to PM Request.

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

I'm going to keep this relatively simple, short and concise here. He feels 100% like a generic dark, mysterious, edgy anime character with nothing interesting going on at all whatsoever.

Twist is unable to answer specific questions. When he tries to, an anomalous event occurs that blurs his face and distorts his voice to be unrecognizable and indecipherable.

That's way too convenient and forced for its own good.

Twist can instantly know the purpose, function, and method of elimination for any target he sees. The SCP Foundation NEEDS this intel.

This isn't as physically combatively overpowered as Abel, but by sheer function, this already renders him far, far too overpowered and X-Men-ish for his own good.

Anomalous Properties

I think you mean superpowers, because that's essentially what this guy has here.

And last but not least, and this is admittedly an extremely shallow nitpick: I don't like his name. James DEVILian (Devil?) Twist. The words 'Devil' and 'Twist' are in his name. It really doesn't get any more anime edgey than that.

I apologise if this came off as extremely harsh, but I'm not feeling this at all in the slightest.

I'm also not really a fan of edgy anime characters, so I was kinda…completely the wrong person to crit this.

I also completely forgot to cover the plot here, basically because it doesn't have one.

The core plot of this article is the SCP foundation's various attempts to uncover secret information that Twist holds.

This explains literally nothing. He has secrets. What are those secrets? You can make them secretive if you manage to get to drafting this, but for the idea pitch, please give us more information on what those secrets are.

Yeah, I'm sorry if this disappoints, but I have nothing to offer here in terms of suggestions or recommendations or tips. I can only state what I disliked about this piece, and it was essentially all of it. I deeply apologise for that.

I do hope you stay and pursue a work on this site, though, as the Greenlight process can be brutal. Don't be discouraged. The trip to one's first SCP is worth the struggle.

Anywho, I bid you a good day. 👍

P.S. I didn't even acknowledge the crosslink idea. Here's the most generally agreed upon consensus for crosslinking on one's first SCP: don't. Many would view it as trying to ride off the success of more popular articles. You'll need to be a lot more familiar with how things go here first before crosslinking will become a good idea. A first SCP has to be able to stand on its own.

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look.

I'll be honest, I personally don't see this working. Not only is the typical "super suit that messes with the person wearing it" trope extremely commonly seen in popular media and the SCP wiki in general, the portrayal of the Foundation here is questionable to the point of breaking suspension of disbelief for me.

+ show block
– hide block

As a general note, I'm not overly familiar with Anderson Robotics, so I can't comment much about the inclusion of that GoI as the backstory here. For me as a reader the mention of that GoI doesn't contribute meaningfully to the narrative.

My main issue with the premise is pretty much the entirety of this:

Before the foundation could class him as Thaumiel, they tested the suit's abilities and the soldier's control over the suit. After the suit was tested it was found valuable in containing SCP's and helping in raids. He was classed a Thaumiel SCP and assigned to MTF Alpha-9 ("Last Hope") To be trained further and then used in the field. He was shipped to Site-06-3 awaiting deployment.

Having something be useful for containing anomalies is not the same as said something actively containing anomalies. Anomalous gear that could help MTFs fight, for example, would not be considered Thaumiel. The fact that the suit is conveniently "valuable" for containing anomalies despite the person having no Foundation experience whatsoever makes the character/suit seem like a Mary Sue setup. Fast-tracking the guy immediately to Thaumiel and assigning him to Last Hope for training (ideally he should be trained before being put on that MTF, given he's starting from near zero familiarity with Foundation team mechanics) diverts the attention from "feel bad for this guy, he's traumatized by the suit" to "he's just yet another overpowered character solely existing to be shoehorned onto Alpha-9" territory.

The suit's abilities are explained with addendums and mission logs.

I myself am not really interested in a laundry list of the suit's abilities. We already have lots of anomalous/super high-tech suits in the Foundation'verse, including the suit Agent Adams tests in this Resurrection tale: http://www.scpwiki.com/number-one-with-a-bullet

My idea is unique because of two reasons. 1, the SCP's abilities. It's super-human strength, resistance to small bullets and kinetic energy. I have yet to see a robotic SCP with such abilities on the site.

Having the exact specific abilities not be exactly addressed by another suit doesn't really make this unique. It's still fundamentally a suit with a bunch of kind of typical abilities. The reason Adams's suit portrayal works in the aforementioned tale is because the focus isn't on the suit's abilities, but rather Adams's reactions and training and struggles to learn how to cope with wearing the suit in different dangerous scenarios. If the only mechanical difference yours presents is "mine is robotic and has different minutiae qualities", that's not going to be enough to impress the audience.

And 2, It's friendly-ness towards humans and it's will to help them with raids, containment and more that they ask for.

One of the main reasons we don't have much of this sort of thing on the mainsite isn't because no one's ever written them, but rather people have written them but the audience hasn't liked the portrayal. Super powerful convenient friendly suits are kind of lazy writing and reminiscent of childish overpowered characters that aren't taken seriously because of how convenient and easy it is for them to be put in a heroic spotlight where they seemingly can do/experience no wrong.

Part of that is reflected here: the Foundation immediately tests, recruits, and promotes the guy without any sort of suspicion or counseling. The point of the story then seems to be just to set up yet another super cool for no reason character, rather than telling a compelling story that will convince readers to care about the individual on a relatable level. cybersqyd already mentioned this in the post above and it doesn't look like it was properly addressed.

Remember, just because you as the author really really want the Foundation to think your character is cool does not mean it automatically makes sense for in-universe personnel to immediately trust the guy.

Personally I would recommend that you shelve this concept and return to it after you've gotten one or two successful mainsite works submitted. Not only would this require a lot of editing to be workable, it's also concept material that an experienced author would have some difficulty with given both the large number of similar attempts that have gone through the site and the community tendency to regard super suits with skepticism and not intrigue.

If you really want to work with this, I would say definitely remove the Thaumiel rating, remove the Alpha-9 membership, and focus on the Anderson Robotics backstory and the person in the suit as a person and not yet another random asset the Foundation will throw at anomalies without question.

Elevator pitch: For one day reality breaks and this spreads throughout the world. everything starts to be changed. after 24 hours it all stops but secrecy is breached. foundation overdoes amnesthetising the whole world an they have to clean up their mess.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
(This started as a reply above, but jumping down to a new chain so it's not so horizontally compressed.)

I suppose something I could do is to eliminate all narrative/reasoning portions from this concept and only put down what he is and what he is capable of doing.

That would be the opposite of progress here.

There isn't really a section in the template for SCP Abilities.

Correct. There is a reason for this. SCPs are not merely strange things with lists of abilities, they are stories.

+ my suggestion for where to go from here
- Chisel until the parts that don't look like a statue are gone.

First things first, pitfall wise, you're 100% looking at walking a tightrope over Edgelord Canyon here. This guy could easily tip over into the abyss of edgy 90's comic book characters that have names spelled with statistically disproportionate quantities of "x"s and "y"s… but if you can make this guy a rounded, grounded character it could actually work.

I can see a glimmer of raw diamond here, but the gem metaphor applies heavily: the jeweler's task is all about precisely cutting away the extraneous material to leave only the most interesting parts.
Reading through what you've said so far, I spot the makings of a viable elevator pitch that makes my ears perk up-

  • "He doesn't see someone's destiny. He sees their "supposed" destiny, or what it is that they were meant to do in life, the thing that they are driven towards or driven to do."
  • "wears an assortment of anomalous artifacts that are melded with his body."
  • Jack is a part of Twist's mind
  • the general idea of him pursuing a greater, possibly even benevolent, goal in this hunt he's on

The first one is all the anomaly you need to set you up with an interesting character: A guy with a simple but potent ability chasing pieces of a domino chain that could lead to a cataclysmic end scenario that isn't necessarily going to happen.

Not necessarily suggesting any direct/overt connection, but I immediately jump to SCP-4239- (one of the GAW's Misters Against Weed, Mr. Destiny). His anomaly enables people to find their destiny in this exact sense- not a predetermined fate, but rather their driving purpose and their potential for doing the right thing at the right time to set further things in motion. Mostly just pointing it out as an interesting opposite thematically, but there's also big-picture potential for them to at least have intersecting interests at some point.

But back to the current idea: to riff off of what Cybersquid said, the interest here for me lives in that ambiguous intersection and contrast of "Twist is a ruthless murderer chasing shadows that might only exist in his own head" and "Twist is an anti-hero who will stop at nothing to prevent the destruction of the world". He's not an all-knowing unstoppable monster… just a man who sees a little more than others, with an obsession that may or may not be justified, and a few tricks up his sleeve.

Regarding the grab bag of grafted-on anomalies, the bootleg cyborg thing is a vibe I'm personally a fan of in general, but in this case keep it grounded. A laundry list of abilities isn't going to interest the audience, and pulling out a new gadget every two minutes to do exactly whatever he wants is cartoon supervillain territory. Use simple things in a clever way, though and you paint a picture of a resourceful and competent threat building on past successes.

You've got a great way to organically tie this part of his concept back into the rest, making it even more interesting and playing up that "magnificent bastard" aspect at the same time: What if he can see the potential in things, too? You could get a ton of milage out of having most of his collection being the sort of thing you'd see on the Anomalous Items List, combined in clever ways because he can see their potential. This can complicate his moral standing in odd ways, too- say, he knows that item A vastly increases his ability to stop the cataclysm, but item A is a piece of paratech in the head of a particular unimportant CotBG member. It's nothing special, but it has to be that one.

More flashy components could also be used to hint at past exploits, or even as the basis for tales in themselves. One suggestion I'd throw out is that SCP-748-5 instances (I won't spoil the non-essential details) have integrated phasing tech- the catch being that their tech self-destructs on termination so the unit would have to be alive functional during the transplant process, and that it's probably not going to be the most stable item in his kit even if both he and the device survive the process.

Lastly, while the "tightrope over Edgelord Canyon" warning remains the big flashing red danger sign here, I'd strongly recommend embracing the edginess a little bit if you go the tale series route- like there's some great potential for zombie-stomping action-horror here if you can keep it on the rails in the process.
